image.name: Novva Data Centers
image.description: Novva Data Centers is a CIM Group-backed U.S. wholesale and colocation data-center platform serving hyperscale, cloud, artificial-intelligence and enterprise customers across the western United States. The company was founded in 2020 with funding from CIM and Novva's founders, received an additional US$355 million of CIM growth equity in 2022 and announced US$2 billion of new financing with CIM in 2025. Novva announced on November 29, 2023 that it had acquired the 400 Paul Avenue campus in San Francisco and now markets the site as Novva Data Centers–San Francisco. The campus had been acquired by a CIM/1547 joint venture in August 2017, entered construction in April 2018 and was marketed at approximately 24 MW before Novva's acquisition; Novva currently markets 36 MW on the 7.5-acre site. The seller, exact Novva closing date, retained CIM/1547 site economics and independently verified commissioned capacity are not publicly disclosed. CIM remains the current manager-level sponsor of Novva; its fund, vehicle and ownership percentage are not public. 400 Paul is an underlying facility and alias rather than a separate PortCo. No later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

image.name: Bolder Industries
image.description: Bolder Industries is a U.S. circular-materials infrastructure platform that converts end-of-life tires into recovered carbon black, pyrolysis oil, steel and energy for tire, rubber, plastics and other industrial customers. The company was founded in 2011 and is headquartered in Boulder, Colorado. Its operating and development footprint includes Maryville, Missouri, Terre Haute, Indiana and Antwerp, Belgium; those facilities and projects are not separate PortCos. CIM was an early investor and expanded its investment in October 2021. Tiger Infrastructure Partners completed a growth investment on February 10, 2025 through a recapitalization in which CIM participated, so Tiger joined rather than replaced CIM. Both sponsors remain current based on manager portfolio and board evidence. Their exact funds, vehicles, stakes and control rights, and CIM's original entry date, are not publicly disclosed. No later platform sale, exit, insolvency or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

image.name: IENTC Telecomunicaciones
aliases: IENTC, S. de R.L. de C.V.
image.description: IENTC Telecomunicaciones is a Mexican telecommunications operator that owns and operates fiber infrastructure serving carrier, corporate and residential customers. The company provides dedicated internet access, data transport, dark fiber, fiber-to-the-home and telephony services and reports approximately 37,500 kilometres of fiber across Mexico. Its legal name is IENTC, S. de R.L. de C.V., and it is headquartered in Santiago de Querétaro. CIM-managed funds invested in the first quarter of 2022 and retain 45% aggregate equity with board representation; CIM Real Assets & Credit Fund separately reported a 21.3% interest in IENTC 1, LLC. IENTC 2 debt was repaid in full during fiscal 2025, but the equity investment remained active. The exact legal chain between IENTC 1 and the Mexican operating company, the second CIM vehicle and the non-CIM shareholder identities are not publicly disclosed. IENTC is unrelated to the separate Sempra company Infraestructura Energética Nova. No CIM equity exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Permanent Power Company
image.subsector: Utility-scale solar, battery storage and transmission
image.description: Permanent Power Company is a CIM Group-backed U.S. power-infrastructure platform that owns and develops utility-scale solar generation, battery storage and transmission assets. SEC filings identify Permanent Power Company, LLC as the renamed former Westlands Electric Power Company, LLC. At March 31, 2026, CIM Opportunity Zone Fund held approximately 66.7% of the company, including its direct interest and the interest held through COZ 1, while other CIM-affiliated entities held the remaining 33.3%. CIM launched the Permanent Power brand in May 2026 with 652 MW of operating solar, 360 MW/1,440 MWh of battery storage and 15 miles of transmission, plus the Grape and Daylight projects in construction or construction-ready development. Westlands Solar Park is the California site/master plan beneath Permanent Power, and Aquamarine is its first 250 MW utility-scale solar project rather than a separate portfolio company. The Westlands development lineage began in 2014, construction started in 2020 and Aquamarine entered commercial operation in late 2021. The exact rename effective date, company headquarters and identities within the 33.3% CIM-affiliate block are not publicly disclosed. No third-party sale, change of control or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.description: Sunrise Renewables is a staffed Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners development platform for utility-scale solar and battery-storage projects in the United States. Public evidence does not support the prior CI IV ownership, a green-hydrogen scope, a Kentucky headquarters or a 2022 CIP entry date. A New York business address appears in filings, but the formal headquarters is not publicly disclosed. No operating project, platform sale, ownership transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.description: Toqlukuti'k Wind & Hydrogen is a pre-FID wind, hydrogen and green-ammonia development in Newfoundland and Labrador held through Toqlukuti'k Wind and Hydrogen Limited. That lapse impaired the development right but did not establish an equity sale, cancellation or owner exit. No later ownership transfer, financing close, FID, construction start or signed pending transaction was identified through August 19, 2026. TQK facilities and land rights remain components of this one project-company record.

image.name: Vineyard Offshore
image.description: Vineyard Offshore is Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners' U.S. offshore-wind development platform, established in 2022 with federal lease interests held through CI IV. Its disclosed portfolio includes Excelsior Wind within OCS-A 0544 and Vineyard Northeast within OCS-A 0522, as well as other east- and west-coast developments. Vineyard Northeast is the lease and project identity for OCS-A 0522, whose current lessee is Vineyard Northeast LLC; Vineyard Wind 2 is a proposed project of up to 1.2 GW inside that lease, not a separate manager-level company. A 50/50 Avangrid and CIP joint venture won the lease in 2018 and it became effective on April 1, 2019. On January 10, 2022, a CI IV vehicle acquired Avangrid's interest and obtained 100% of the lease rights. Massachusetts provisionally selected 800 MW in September 2024, but Vineyard Offshore withdrew the bid on December 20, 2024 after Connecticut made no offshore-wind selection. The lease remains active, while FAST-41 permitting is paused to April 1, 2027; no PPA, FID, financing close, construction start, lease surrender, sale, CIP exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026. Vineyard Northeast, Vineyard Wind 2, Excelsior Wind and their lease SPVs are consolidated beneath this one platform record; Vineyard Wind 1 remains distinct.

image.name: Autopista Arco Norte, S.A. de C.V.
image.description: Autopista Arco Norte, S.A. de C.V., commonly known as Arco Norte, operates a 223-kilometer federal user-pay toll road across the State of Mexico, Hidalgo, Tlaxcala and Puebla. The concession was granted on December 21, 2005 and is scheduled to expire on December 20, 2065. IDEAL contributed its 99% Arco Norte interest to Promotora Punta Cometa, S.A. de C.V. in the partnership that closed on December 22, 2016; at close, CPP Investments held 29% of that vehicle and Ontario Teachers' held 20%, alongside IDEAL and a small Inbursa affiliate interest. Later FIDEAL restructuring changed the direct capitalization beneath the road, so current manager look-through percentages are not publicly disclosed and the 2016 percentages should not be presented as direct concessionaire stakes. Ontario Teachers' continues to list Arco Norte separately from IDEAL, supporting treatment as its own manager-level infrastructure holding. No manager exit, concession transfer, termination or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026. Promotora Punta Cometa is the upstream holding vehicle; IDEAL Group and Pacifico Sur remain separate investments.
